steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Generously grease a 2-quart baking dish.
Arrange apples in an even layer in the prepared baking dish. Combine ½ cup sugar, ½ cup pecans, and cinnamon in a bowl; sprinkle over apples.

Combine remaining 1 cup sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl until well mixed. Whisk evaporated milk, melted butter, and beaten egg together in a separate bowl until combined; stir into flour mixture until smooth. Pour batter over apples; sprinkle with remaining ¼ cup pecans.
Bake in the preheated oven for 55 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Pecan Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This apple pecan cobbler recipe features thinly sliced apples, sugared pecans, and a tender cake batter, topped with extra pecans for a nutty treat.

review.reviewBody: YUMMYLICIOUS! The first two times I made it, I inadvertedly used baking soda instead of baking powder. I rectified my mistake next time I baked it and used baking powder as the recipe calls for. I found that the soda works SO MUCH BETTER. I also add nutmeg, cloves, ginger and raisins. I have an apple tree that has given me abundant fruit so I have baked this cobbler MANY, MANY TIMES. I get nothing but raves.

Very tasty! I wouldn't really call it a cobbler though. It was definitely more cake like. A few changes I will make next time. I would recommend using 6-7 apples instead of 4. I used pretty decent sized apples and it was about 75% cake and 25% apples. I added additional cinnamon and coated the pecans on top in some butter and brown sugar before sprinkling. Overall it was a big hit on Christmas Eve!

My friends and family love this cobbler. I’ve made numerous times. The last time I made I sliced apples very thin and seasoned with cinnamon and brown sugar and let sit for 30 min before adding flour mixture. I double the batch and once it came out the oven the entire cobbler was gone in 30 minutes.

Delicious!!! I decided to double the batter recipe. I goofed and ended up not having evaporated milk. So I used some old buttermilk which almost turned to a "clotting" disaster saved by adding about 1/4 cup of whole milk to the final batter mixture. I also added 1/2 tsp each of vanilla and almond extract to the wet ingredients. I know I don't like things too sweet, so I only used about a 1/4 cup sugar with the apples (4 medium to large Fuji) and 1 cup of sugar to the batter (again I was doubling the batter; all the batter ingredients were doubled except the butter, I used a whole stick). Still came out sweet. This has go to be the best dessert I've made, and I do make some great banana bread. Even my kid says this is better. A winner for sure. I'll be sure to stock up on evaporated milk from now on?? (I usually don't like nuts in my food, so I used 1/4 cup of pecan pieces (for cookies) over the apples, and didn't add any on top of the batter; I used a 13*9 pan). Enjoy!

I did not make any changes, but I would make an extra amount of the biscuit mixture, maybe 1/2 more to cover all of the apples. Also it needs to bake way longer than the recipe calls for to ensure the topping is done.

Oh, boy! I read the most useful comments. I used 5 cups unpeeled Granny Smith apples. I doubled the cobbler topping ingredients. I baked for 1 hour and about 20 minutes. Finally, I sampled a tiny slice. Oh,boy!

I love apples so I had to try this and was not disappointed. I did alter it a bit because I think that's the purpose of reading user reviews. I used brown sugar in the apples (3 granny's and 2 golden delicious) and some maple syrup, a little bit of water and flour plus the cinnamon and mixed the apples up before adding the topping. I decreased the sugar in the batter and used 1/3 cup of white and 1/3 cup of brown and added 2 more tbsp of evaporated milk. I also added the pecans (finely chopped, just a personal preference) to the batter instead. I meant to add vanilla but completely forgot and I think it turned out fine without it. The cooking time was pretty accurate for my oven. I love what one reviewer said, "Call it cake, call it cobbler. Who cares? It's delicious!" Agreed!

I doubled recipe, then halved the sugar. 
Was plenty of sweet flavor for us.
Really good with homemade ice cream, and was a hit at Thanksgiving.
It was delicious. I used walnuts in place of pecans, and half and half in place of evaporated milk, because of what I had on hand. Used a 9X9 square baking pan.

Marvelously delicious cobbler. Like another poster, I doubled the recipe, cooked it an additional ten minutes in a 13x9 dish, and it was perfect. I reduced the total sugar by about 1/2 cup, and I'll reduce it a little more next time. I like to taste the tartness of the apples. The pecans (my favorite nut!) add a delightful crunch to the cobbler, too. If you like a lot of cinnamon, you might add more than the recipe calls for, but I found the amount in the recipe perfect as I don't like the cinnamon to overpower the flavor of the apples. I will be making this again tonight to bring in to my coworkers tomorrow. It's delicious!
This recipe is great just just the way it is written. I ended up doubling it and making three small ones, because of this I had to reduce the time a tad. Everyone enjoyed it!
Great flavor. Nice crunch from pecans.
I did not have pecans, so I used almond slivers,,,,,,,,,,,,,I was so good!
Easy and tasty. Use as many apple slices as your pan will hold. I agree that adding cinnamon to the topping ups the flavor, and I added a sprinkle of nutmeg.
This recipe is really great added a little bit more cinnamon but overall everything was good
A very nice dessert. I do like brown sugar on the top of the pecans. Also, White vinegar is listed in the ingredients but does not state in making the mixtures where and when to add?

Made it today and used half sugar and half splenda. Also added some raisins.

Fantastic ! We can't stop eating it !

giving it a 5 rating
M!m M!m Good! Made with a 1/2 cup sugar less tonight with a nice salad top with an egg & that was dinner.
A great recipe. Used 2% milk instead of evaporated milk. Family loved it.
Not exactly my idea of a cobbler with more moisture to blend with the ice cream, but the more cake-like texture made a divine coffee cake accompaniment with coffee the next morning.
